issues.legal_issue: Income from conducting a business can constitute property held under trust for purposes of the charitable-income exemption.
material_facts: The organization earned income from conducting kuries or chit funds and from money lending.
The governing documents provided for raising funds through those activities to advance the organization’s stated objects.
issues.conclusion: A business is property within the meaning of the charitable-income exemption provisions, and the business activities here were held under trust; those findings alone did not establish that the income was exempt.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on section 11(1)(a) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and noted that sections 11(4) and 13(1)(bb) also show that business is property. It followed Commissioner of Income Tax v. Krishna Warrier.

predicates.charitable_tax_exemption_claim: The proceeding includes a claim to exempt income on the ground that it is held for charitable purposes.
predicates.income_earned_from_business: The organization earned income by carrying on a business.

issues.definition: When an organization claims charitable tax exemption for income earned through business, that income is treated as property held under trust.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a trust is for charitable purposes is determined by considering all its governing objects, except an object clearly shown never to have been intended for pursuit.
material_facts: The governing documents contained several objects, including objects concerning charity, education, industry, and public good; the documents were later amended to refer to medical relief and other matters of public good.
The organization argued that its actual activities, rather than the full range of objects in its governing documents, should determine its status.
The Court found no clear evidence that the non-charitable objects had never been intended to be undertaken.
issues.conclusion: The Court assessed the organization’s charitable status by reference to all the objects in its governing documents and did not disregard the objects challenged as non-charitable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Tennent Plays Ltd. v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue, Incorporated Council of Law Reporting for England and Wales v. Attorney-General and Commissioners of Inland Revenue, and Rex v. The Special Commissioners of Income-Tax. It distinguished Commissioner of Income-Tax, Kerala v. Dharmodayam Co., explaining that an object may be ignored if clear evidence shows it was never intended to be undertaken.

rule.if: charitable_status_case and objects_in_governing_instrument and not clear_evidence_object_never_intended

predicates.charitable_status_case: The proceeding requires a determination whether an organization or trust is for charitable purposes.
predicates.objects_in_governing_instrument: The organization’s governing instrument states the purposes for which it was created.
predicates.clear_evidence_object_never_intended: Clear evidence shows that a stated object was never intended to be undertaken.

issues.definition: When charitable status depends on governing objects, all stated objects are considered unless clear evidence shows that a particular object was never intended to be pursued.

issues.legal_issue: Income from business held for charitable purposes is not exempt when the governing objects include non-charitable purposes, the income may be applied among those purposes at discretion, and profit-making activity is not restricted.
material_facts: The organization earned income from kuries or chit funds and money lending, and its business was held under trust.
The original objects included industry and public good; the amended objects included medical relief and other matters of public good, with public good remaining a distinct object.
The governing documents permitted the income to be applied among the objects at the organization’s discretion and did not restrict profit-making activity in pursuing the relevant objects.
No definite part of the business or its income was confined to charitable purposes.
issues.conclusion: The income was not exempt: the claim failed in full for the years governed by the original objects, and the later amendments did not change that result.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(15) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, defines charitable purpose to include specified purposes and the advancement of other objects of general public utility only when they do not involve carrying on an activity for profit. Under section 11(1)(a), the income must be held for charitable purposes. The Court applied Sole Trustee, Loka Sikshana Trust v. Commissioner of Income-Tax and Commissioner of Income-Tax, Kerala v. Cochin Chamber of Commerce and Industry for the inference that an unrestricted business activity ordinarily involves an activity for profit. It relied on Mohammed Ibrahim Raza v. Commissioner of Income-Tax and East India Industries (Madras) Private Limited v. Commissioner of Income-Tax for the consequence of income being available to both charitable and non-charitable objects. It explained that Commissioner of Income-Tax, Kerala v. Dharmodayam Co. turned on different facts.

rule.if: charitable_tax_exemption_claim and business_income_held_for_trust and noncharitable_object_present and income_discretionarily_applicable_to_all_objects and profit_making_activity_unrestricted

predicates.charitable_tax_exemption_claim: The organization claims an exemption for income on the ground that it is held for charitable purposes.
predicates.business_income_held_for_trust: The income was earned from a business held under the organization’s governing arrangement for its stated purposes.
predicates.noncharitable_object_present: The governing objects include at least one purpose that is not charitable.
predicates.income_discretionarily_applicable_to_all: The organization may apply the relevant income among the stated objects at its discretion, without confining a definite part to charitable purposes.
predicates.profit_making_activity_unrestricted: The governing arrangement places no restriction on profit-making activity in pursuing the relevant objects.

issues.definition: A charitable-income exemption is denied when business income held for an organization’s purposes may be applied to both charitable and non-charitable objects and profit-making activity is unrestricted.
